reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent, sole pass — proportionate to a test-and-docs change with no production code; it mutation-tested three variants of the re-credit branch and independently re-measured both published rows

records.finding: The negative half of the re-credit test did not discriminate the branch's family guard. Asserting only the invalid sum kills a mutation that re-queues the metrics slice, but not the one that matters: deleting the `if p.Name == "biz_dropped_events_total"` guard folds every failed point's value into dropCounts and the test stayed green.
records.evidence: Reviewer's mutation C left the suite green while minting biz_dropped_events_total{reason=""} = 14901 — a transaction count plus a money amount — on the next flush.
records.reason: The test asserts the whole drop-point set against {invalid:1, export:1}. Mutation C now fails with map[:14901 export:1 invalid:1], and mutations A and B still fail. I had reported this as proved on both sides after testing two mutations; the third was the one worth proving.

records.finding: The de-dup reset reallocated a ~1 MB twoGenSet every block. The allocation was outside the timed region but its GC work was not, in a benchmark whose stated purpose is to price only the accept path. ADR-0015 asks for clear() over reallocation in loops.
records.evidence: Reviewer measured 1388.5 ns and 154 MB peak RSS as written against 1335.5 ns and 130 MB with clear(), identical B/op and allocs/op — about 3.8% of the published figure was the benchmark's own bookkeeping.
records.reason: clear(em.dedup.cur) replaces the reallocation; cur holds one block's 4096 keys against a 65536 capacity so it never rotates and prev stays nil. Numbers re-measured after the change.

records.finding: The note quoted 'delivered 49152 outcomes for 187820 Record calls' as what the conservation assertion reports, but b.N is host- and timing-dependent and will not reproduce.
records.evidence: Reviewer's run of the same reverted code produced 'delivered 49152 outcomes for 541564 Record calls'.
records.reason: Quotes only the invariant half — 49152 is the pool size and is exact — and says the call count is whatever the run reached.

records.finding: The diff published a second unreconciled 'accepted, one core' figure: README says 2.3 microseconds from BenchmarkRecordParallel at -cpu 1, the new row says 1,525 ns for the same wording, and the branch had deleted the sentence that reconciled them.
records.evidence: README.md:305 against docs/performance.md:497, with 'The honest accept figures are the BenchmarkRecordParallel table above' removed by this diff.
records.reason: A paragraph now names the difference: BenchmarkRecordParallel runs a live flusher so each call carries its amortised export share, while this benchmark uses WithFlushInterval(0) and drains with the timer stopped. Two questions, two numbers.
